item.title: Executive Director
item.description: WREA Executive Director Job Description Office Administration: accountable to the WREA Board of Directors establish office hours in consultation with the WREA President oversee the WREA office as outlined in the WREA Policy Handbook negotiate contracts for equipment review insurance requirements for the WREA review all contracts on an annual basis oversee the purchase of capital equipment maintain confidentiality of membership records and other WREA business respond to member requests and complaints participate in Condo Association meetings and related Condo office issues proficient in Word, Excel, Outlook, Power Point and Cloud based document receptacle Staff Supervision: abide by personnel policies approved by the WREA Board of Directors employ and terminate office staff as outlined in the WREA Policy Handbook supervise office staff conduct annual staff reviews Fiscal Management: fiscally responsible to the WREA Board of Directors and the WREA Foundation Board of Trustees oversee fiscal records, completion of Compilation Report, and the timely filing of all tax reports work closely with the WREA’s banker, accountant and office staff in making financial decisions for both the WREA and the WREA Foundation oversee and assure compliance with adopted budget make recommendations for financial adjustments as may be necessary primary responsibility in facilitating both the WREA and the WREA Foundation annual compilation Association Meetings and Goals: develop a marketing plan for the association assist in annual convention and delegate assembly planning assist with meeting arrangements, agenda and program development for district meetings WREA Board Activities and Committees: assume a leadership role in working with the WREA President, the WREA Board of Directors and Standing Committees to promote the WREA’s purpose, missions, goals and to implement policies and programs accountable to the WREA President and the WREA Board of Directors collaborate with the Team R.I.S.E. Committee in recruiting, retaining and regaining members assure agreements with member benefit partners are honored assist in agenda preparations assist committees in goal-making and review work with the WREA Board of Directors to develop policy responsible for membership records: posting of new members, dues payments and membership status Legislative Activity: lobby and prepare legislative testimony for hearings and attend hearings as needed register as a lobbyist for WREA assure that the WREA has liaisons to critical organizations, advocacy groups and agencies with common legislative interests prepare legislative materials in coordination with the Legislative Committee prepare legislative alerts on behalf of the Legislative Committee and the WREA Board of Directors collaborate with the contracted WREA Lobbyist and the Legislative Committee to develop the survey for each biennial session oversee the development of biennial legislative goals and priorities meet regularly with SAA Board of Directors to determine legislative priorities Communication Activity: oversee website updating communicate pertinent information to members as needed work in conjunction with member benefit partners on member communications resolve member benefit complaints develop resource materials as needed for association activities oversee the production of all association printed and electronic materials provide oversight and review of WREA communications and publications assist with Leadership News, Red Apple Express, Green Apple Express, WREA News email blasts, and campaigns oversee the Retirement Seminars and distribution of promotional materials Litigation (when involved): oversee litigation as directed by the WREA Board of Directors work with WREA attorney in the coordination and analysis of legal proceedings Outreach Activity: represent the WREA in all external matters attend unit meetings as requested provide information of interest to retired and prospective members maintain relationships with other agencies, organizations and coalitions monitor the Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS) and maintain contact with the Department of Employee Trusts Funds (ETF) and the State of Wisconsin Investment Board (SWIB) maintain relationships with state agencies and other public officials for the association assist in tabulating convention and district meeting evaluations Issues Analysis: study issues pertaining to the WREA goals and purposes initiate the development of organizational planning and activities regarding issues of critical interest to the WREA including pension, education, health care reform and economic security As an employee of WREA, the Executive Director will perform other duties as assigned by the WREA President or Board of Directors. EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR VACANCY The Wisconsin Retired Educators’ Association (WREA) Board of Directors is announcing a vacancy for the position of Executive Director. The WREA is an issue-driven organization representing the interests of Wisconsin’s retired educational community. The WREA Office is in Middleton, WI and serves the statewide membership of more than 6,000 retired educators. Essential to successfully carrying out this full-time role is a strong commitment to supporting public education and to Prek-16 educators. The cover letter must share the applicant’s knowledge of WREA, a non-profit, non-partisan entity. Please share how you can support and promote WREA’s mission. The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and manages the affairs of the Association, implements policies and directives of the Board, supervises and evaluates the work of staff. The Executive Director develops and maintains relationships with affiliated local, state and national organizations and a registered lobbyist for WREA. Salary: Based on Experience plus negotiated benefits. Responsibilities of the Executive Director Include: Assume a leadership role in working with the President, Board of Directors, Executive Council, and WREA Foundation Trustees to promote the association’s purposes and goals and implement its policies and programs Coordinate lobbying efforts with the chair of the legislative committee and be a registered lobbyist Serve as Membership Committee chairperson per By-laws, to help maintain its membership, and promote membership growth Manage the WREA office, including the employment of other staff Assume responsibility for communications and publications of WREA Manage the daily financial affairs of WREA See job description below for details. Click the link to apply https://wrea.net/page/WREAExecutiveDirector Required Qualifications : Degree in Public Administration, Educational Administration, or related educational field Understanding of 401(c) (4) nonprofit organization Excellent written and verbal communication skills Experience in developing, writing, and executing a strategic plan Note: For more information about WREA, please visit our website at www.wrea.net . Required Application Packet must include : A cover letter that includes your knowledge of the Wisconsin Retired Educators’ Association and the public employee pension. A resume which reflects your qualifications, experiences and skills for the position. The names, street addresses, telephone numbers and email addresses of three references. Application Packet must be submitted by: October 21, 2026 Incomplete or late applications will not be considered Please note that given the anticipated interest in this position, the names of applicants may be released at some time during the hiring process and there will be background checks. The WREA is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on sex, creed, color, national origin, disability, age or sexual orientation.
